title: MAC Addresses and the Link Layer

questions.prompt: How many bits is a MAC address?
questions.explanation: A MAC address is 48 bits, written as six hexadecimal pairs (e.g. 00:1A:2B:3C:4D:5E).

options.text: Resolves an IPv4 address to a MAC address on the local network
Assigns IP addresses to new devices
Routes packets between the internet's networks

questions.explanation: ARP maps a known local IPv4 address to the MAC address needed to build and deliver a frame. IPv6 uses NDP for the same job.

questions.prompt: Which statements correctly contrast MAC and IP addresses? Select all that apply.

options.text: MAC is a layer-2 address used for delivery on one local link
IP is a routable layer-3 address for end-to-end delivery
The MAC address is rewritten at each hop
The IP address is rewritten at each hop while the MAC stays the same

questions.explanation: MAC is local/layer-2 and changes each hop; IP is routable/layer-3 and normally stays end-to-end. Option D reverses the truth.

questions.prompt: A network device that learns which host is on which port and forwards frames only to the correct port is called a ____.
questions.explanation: A switch builds a MAC address table from the source MAC of incoming frames and forwards to the matching port, unlike a hub which floods every port.

questions.prompt: Order the ARP steps when host A (same subnet) wants to reach host B and has no cached entry.

items.text: A knows B's IP but not B's MAC
A builds the frame and sends it to B

questions.explanation: ARP broadcasts a request, the owner replies with its MAC, the sender caches the mapping, then delivers the frame directly.

questions.prompt: Match each term to its description.

pairs.right: The link-layer PDU wrapping an IP packet
The vendor prefix in a MAC address
Hosts a broadcast frame reaches without a router

questions.explanation: A frame carries the packet at layer 2; the OUI identifies the vendor; a broadcast domain is bounded by routers; NDP does neighbor resolution in IPv6.
